key_insight: InstructSAM reformulates instruction-driven multi-instance segmentation as a set-structured query prediction problem and connects VLM reasoning to SAM3 via an explicit reasoning-to-instance query interface, using a bank of learnable instance queries to produce masks for arbitrary natural-language instructions.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between language-guided reasoning and mask generation to enable reliable, multi-instance segmentation from arbitrary instructions without ad-hoc interfaces or per-task engineering.
method: Set-structured query prediction: treat each target instance as a query in a set so the model outputs an unordered collection of instance predictions.
Reasoning-to-instance query interface: inject a bank of learnable instance queries into a Vision–Language Model (VLM) and contextualize them with instruction and visual features.
SAM3 integration: pass contextualized instance queries to SAM3 to generate high-quality instance masks conditioned on the instruction-driven queries.
impact: Makes interactive, instruction-driven segmentation practical and modular—useful for annotation tools, human–robot interaction, and multimodal research—by unifying VLM reasoning with a state-of-the-art segmentation backbone.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: Image + instruction → VLM → learnable instance queries → SAM3 → multiple masks
Before/after examples: same image with different natural-language instructions producing different sets of instance masks
Query visualization: graphic showing a bank of learnable queries being contextualized by instruction and image features
Comparison chart: qualitative/quantitative gains vs. baselines (accuracy, flexibility, number of instances handled)
paper_title: InstructSAM: Segment Any Instance with Any Instructions
paper_authors: Yuqian Yuan, Wentong Li, Zhaocheng Li, Yutong Lin, Juncheng Li
